ch-007.txt: Blackmon chapters III-XII and XIII-XVI are detailed US case histories (antebellum industrial slavery, John Pace's Alabama slave farm, the 1903 peonage indictments and trials, the Atlanta and Birmingham convict systems, mine disasters) whose subject is the American South 1865-1945. They are outside the post-colonial African modules; the course uses Blackmon only as Module 3 diaspora context and as the documented contrast to the Willie Lynch hoax, for which the introduction, chapter II (legal origins of convict leasing), and the ending chapters (XVII freedom, epilogue) are sufficient. Not read in full on purpose; findings from this book are limited accordingly.
